text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard told Parliament yesterday the Government, under proposed amendments to the Commonwealth's native title legislation, will significantly boost its powers to intervene in native title claims in a bid to see that key development projects are not delayed. Page 1.

Following the release to Parliament of the royal commission report into the crash of a Seaview plane in 1994, Federal Transport Minister John Sharp conceded yesterday he could not guarantee the safety of air travellers, saying he did not have confidence in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority to protect the travelling public. Page 3.

The Murray-Darling Commission said yesterday emergency compensation would be provided to flood-affected landowners in Victoria and New South Wales after deciding to relieve pressure on the swollen Hume Dam, east of Albury-Wodonga, by prolonging its current level of overflow for another two weeks. Page 3.

Following backbench concerns about its impact on medical students already in the system, the Federal Government's controversial Budget plan to limit the number of GPs, which was designed to save more than A$500 million over four years, could be modified bfore it is even introduced to Parliament. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following a report by the Commission of Inquiry, headed by John Staunton QC, which found the Seaview Air crash two years ago that killed nine people followed a combination of incompetence, lies and systematic ignorance by aviation safety authorities and Saview, Federal Transport Minister John Sharp said yesterday he was not sure the Civil Aviation Safety Authority could protect air travellers from operators like Seaview. Page 1.

Following comments by Opposition Leader Kim Beazley calling for Prime Minister John Howard to condemn the views of Queensland Independent MP Pauline Hanson, Howard yesterday mounted a comprehensive defence of his commitment to racial equality and a non-dicriminatory immigration policy, but he did say people were entitled to attack present immigration levels without being branded as "bigots or racists". Page 1.

In a move that signals the partial privatisation of the University of Melbourne, Australia's second oldest university, the facility is set to create an elite A$120 million private teaching and research institute that would offer foreign Governments, international agencies and corporations across the Asia-Pacific region advice on energy and environment issues. Page 1.

As Super League warned it would begin a fresh raid on Australian Rugby League players and clubs tomorrow, Optus last night announced it would fund the struggling ARL competition for the next five years in a deal believed to be worth A$174 million. ARL charman Ken Arthurson said the deal restored his faith in the future of the ARL's competition. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following warnings from members of his own backbench that the racism debate is resulting in a backlash against Asians, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday praised the contribution of Asian immigrants to Australian society and stressed his abhorrence of rcial intolerance.
Page 1.

A Federal inquiry, headed by Commissioner James Staunton, has found the Seaview Air flagship which crashed in the Tasman Sea killing nine passengers was "seriously overloaded" and has recommended criminal charges be considered against John Green, the airine's owner. Page 1.

In a move which effectively amounts to a discontinuance of the past bipartisanship, Prime Minister John Howard effectively ruled out any practical Government response to an inquiry into the forced separation of thousands of Aboriginal children from their amilies, saying there was little to be gained from a re-examination of past policy. Page 1.

Following a record number of animal cruelty investigations reported in its annual report and concern at practices such as cockfighting, the RSPCA, Australia's largest animal shelter, targeted Sydney's Asian community. The RSPCA believes Asian immigrants, articularly non-English speakers, are responsible for part of the increase in animal cruelty investigations. Page 3.
THE AGE

After 150 nurses at Dandenong Hospital tested a "strong positive" to the tuberculosis test, nurses yesterday criticised the Victorian Government's decision earlier this year to close Fairfield Hospital, the State's infectious diseases hospital, and complaned about a lack of isolation beds, inadequate infection-control procedures and education. Page A1.

Victorian Health Minister Rob Knowles yesterday announced an investigation into allegations that public hospitals are being forced to manipulate waiting list figures to secure funding under the case-mix system, after the Australian Medical Association andthe Australian Nursing Federation backed the claims in public statements. Page A1.

Following a lengthy debate in the Government party room and a challenge from Opposition Leader Kim Beazley to show leadership on the issue, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday told Parliament that the Liberal and National parties were committed to racialequality and racial tolerance and supported a non-discriminatory immigration policy. Page A1.

Although Prime Minister John Howard yesterday refused a Coalition party room vote on a motion to dump the Private Member's Bill to overturn the Northern Territory's euthanasia legislation, South Australian MP Christine Gallus said she was considering askig Parliament to vote that the Bill not proceed, in a move which would appeal to many MPs and Senators who have voiced concerns about the Bill. Page A3.
